original_question: If K is an infinite field whose absolute Galois group GK is prosolvable, must K be ample?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Question II: "Is every infinite field with prosolvable G_K ample?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's intended problem very closely: it has the correct ambient object (an infinite field K), the correct hypothesis on the absolute Galois group G_K (prosolvable), and the correct conclusion (that K should be ample). In substance, it is essentially the same question as the paper's official formulation in Section 4.1, Question II.
missing_details: The notation G_K should be made explicit as the absolute Galois group Gal(K^sep/K).
The group-theoretic hypothesis should be read in the profinite sense: prosolvable means an inverse limit of finite solvable groups.
The term ample should be defined, since the question is otherwise not fully stand-alone.
It helps to keep the universal quantifier explicit: the question is whether every infinite field K with this property is ample.
refined_question: Let K be an infinite field, and let G_K = Gal(K^sep/K) be its absolute Galois group. If G_K is prosolvable (i.e. a profinite inverse limit of finite solvable groups), must K be ample, in the sense that every smooth K-curve with a K-rational point has infinitely many K-rational points?
justification: The nearest paper-faithful target is not a broader neighboring problem but the exact Galois-theoretic open problem stated in Section 4.1 as Question II. Your draft is already very close to that wording; the only real omissions are the standard unpacking of the notation G_K, the profinite meaning of prosolvable, and a stand-alone definition of ample. I therefore kept the scope unchanged and only made the statement self-contained.
